findings.explanation: The viewer_certificate block only read cloudfront_default_certificate and minimum_protocol_version from var.viewer_certificate -- no acm_certificate_arn or iam_certificate_id was ever referenced anywhere in the resource, so a caller had no way to attach a custom certificate despite the module exposing minimum_protocol_version (which only has effect alongside a custom cert; CloudFront ignores it when using the default certificate). Worse, the variable's own default was {cloudfront_default_certificate = false, minimum_protocol_version = "TLSv1.2_2019"} with no certificate source at all -- AWS CloudFront requires exactly one of cloudfront_default_certificate=true / acm_certificate_arn / iam_certificate_id to be effectively set, and this default satisfied none of them. terraform validate doesn't catch this (it's a cross-field AWS API constraint, not a schema-level one), so the module's own working example silently relied on a config that would likely fail at apply time against real AWS.
findings.fix: Applied: added acm_certificate_arn (optional(string)) to the viewer_certificate variable type, wired it into the resource's viewer_certificate block, flipped the default to cloudfront_default_certificate = true, and added a validation requiring acm_certificate_arn whenever a caller sets cloudfront_default_certificate = false.
findings.remediation: Wire acm_certificate_arn through from var.viewer_certificate, and either flip the default to cloudfront_default_certificate = true (deployable out of the box) or require callers to always supply a certificate source explicitly.
findings.title: viewer_certificate never wires a custom certificate through, and the module's own default was structurally invalid

findings.explanation: aws_s3_object.error uploads 404.html to the bucket, clearly signaling intent to serve a custom error page, but aws_cloudfront_distribution.s3_distribution has no custom_error_response block mapping a 404 (or 403, which S3 returns via CloudFront+OAI for a missing key) to that object. Without it, a real 404 passes through CloudFront as S3's raw XML error response instead of the custom page -- the uploaded object is created but never actually reachable through the distribution it's meant to back.
findings.remediation: Add a custom_error_response block to the distribution: error_code = 404 (and/or 403), response_code = 404, response_page_path = "/404.html". This is example-specific wiring, not something the module itself should hardcode, since not every consumer will name their error page the same way.
findings.title: 404.html is uploaded but the distribution has no custom_error_response to serve it

suggested_policies.rationale: viewer_certificate requires exactly one effective certificate source (cloudfront_default_certificate=true, acm_certificate_arn, or iam_certificate_id). Setting cloudfront_default_certificate=false with neither of the other two present is a structurally invalid distribution that terraform validate does not catch (the constraint is enforced by the AWS API, not the provider schema) -- generically applicable to any aws_cloudfront_distribution, confirmed via coverage_by_type that none of the 5 existing policies on this resource type (HLD_AWS_023/024/029/112/151) check viewer_certificate completeness.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_AWS_XXX  # use holden next-id --cloud AWS
name: CloudFront viewer_certificate must specify a certificate source
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  aws_cloudfront_distribution.viewer_certificate requires exactly one
  certificate source: cloudfront_default_certificate = true,
  acm_certificate_arn, or iam_certificate_id. Setting
  cloudfront_default_certificate = false with neither of the other two
  present leaves the distribution with no valid certificate source --
  this is a structurally invalid configuration that typically fails at
  apply time against the real CloudFront API rather than at
  `terraform validate`, since the provider schema does not enforce this
  cross-field constraint.
remediation: |
  Either set cloudfront_default_certificate = true, or provide
  acm_certificate_arn (or iam_certificate_id) when
  cloudfront_default_certificate is false.
resources:
  aws_cloudfront_distribution:
    if_equals:
      path: viewer_certificate.cloudfront_default_certificate
      value: false
      then:
        any:
          - path: viewer_certificate.acm_certificate_arn
            not_null: true
          - path: viewer_certificate.iam_certificate_id
            not_null: true
